channelTitle: The photograph on the mantel that explains everything - Part 2
hook: In Part 1, the girl in the pale dress vanished from a moving car. Shaken, the driver knocks on the door anyway - and that's when it gets worse.
storyParts: An older couple answers the door. The driver describes the girl - her dress, her quietness, the coat he lent her. The couple goes very still. Then they show him a photograph on the mantel.

It's their daughter. She died on that stretch of road, they tell him - years ago, on a night just like this one. Every so often, a kind stranger arrives at their door with the same story. Every time, they say the same thing.

The details change by region - Chicago's version is Resurrection Mary, who vanishes outside Resurrection Cemetery and still gets reported to this day. Taxi drivers swear they've picked her up. The address always leads to the cemetery gates.
Folklorists think the story endures because it isn't really about a ghost. It's about the ones who never made it home - and the stranger kind enough to stop, lend a coat, and try to get them there.
So if you're ever driving a lonely road at night and see someone standing at the roadside in the cold - some people say you should still stop. Just maybe check the back seat twice.
moral: Grandma June's takeaway: every old ghost story is a little kindness owed to someone who didn't make it home.
